items.title: Figure Joins NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform as Humanoid Deployment Approaches
items.summary: Figure joined NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform to establish boundaries for increasingly capable AI agents. This initiative combines the OpenShell runtime with Sentry, a monitoring and enforcement layer. Figure's participation focuses on ensuring the safety and trust of humanoid robots operating in homes and workplaces. The platform aims to constrain agent actions through runtime controls rather than just model safeguards. This collaboration provides a foundation for trustworthy agent systems where software decisions translate into physical actions.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Figure Joins NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform as Humanoid Deployment Approaches. This report details Figure's involvement in establishing boundaries for increasingly capable AI agents through a new safety platform. Figure contributed to combining the OpenShell runtime with Sentry, a monitoring and enforcement layer, within the platform. The initiative focuses on ensuring the safety and trust of humanoid robots operating in domestic and professional environments by constraining agent actions through runtime controls instead of solely model safeguards. This collaboration establishes a foundation for trustworthy agent systems where software decisions result in physical actions. This development indicates a push towards implementing robust safety mechanisms for physical AI systems.

items.title: [AINews] AMD buys World Labs for $8.2B, as Atlas solves sparse reconstruction problem for robotics, design and more
items.summary: AMD acquired World Labs for $8.2 billion to gain its AI spatial intelligence capabilities. World Labs developed leading models for images, video, and spatial reconstruction. They recently released Atlas, a new omni model architecture that solves the sparse reconstruction problem through camera view prediction. Atlas has applications across robotics simulation, design, and real-world reconstruction. This acquisition significantly enhances AMD's position in spatial AI and related fields.

This report details the acquisition of World Labs by AMD to integrate its spatial AI capabilities. World Labs developed advanced models for images, video, and spatial reconstruction, culminating in the release of the Atlas model architecture. Atlas addresses the sparse reconstruction problem through the method of camera view prediction. This new architecture has demonstrated applications in robotics simulation, design, and real-world reconstruction. The acquisition significantly expands AMD's standing within the spatial AI sector. This development signals a major advancement in spatial intelligence for various technological applications moving forward.

items.title: A Day in the Life of a Roboticist: Charlie Kemp
items.summary: Charlie Kemp, cofounder and CTO of Hello Robot, develops mobile manipulators to assist people in homes and workplaces. His work focuses on creating assistive robots for older adults and individuals with disabilities, emphasizing close physical interaction. Kemp finds the most rewarding aspects of robotics in seeing software become physical reality and influencing the future. He advises aspiring roboticists to embrace real-world discovery and collaborate with non-robotics experts for impactful applications. His work has involved developing systems that enable meaningful physical assistance for people with mobility impairments.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "A Day in the Life of a Roboticist: Charlie Kemp" details the work of Charlie Kemp, cofounder and CTO of Hello Robot, focusing on the development of mobile manipulators for home and workplace assistance. The research centers on creating assistive robots designed to facilitate close physical interaction for older adults and individuals with disabilities. Kemp's work involved developing systems specifically engineered to enable meaningful physical assistance for people experiencing mobility impairments through advanced mobile manipulation capabilities. This process emphasized the translation of software concepts into tangible physical realities, focusing on the development of systems that provide practical, physical support. The findings highlight the successful integration of robotics into personal care through direct physical interaction. The direction points toward further development in human-robot collaboration for assistive technologies.

items.title: Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze
items.summary: MIT engineers developed a soft, muscle-powered swimming robot using a thin film of gel and genetically engineered muscle cells. These cells are designed to twitch in response to light, causing the robot's fins to flap and propel it through water. By flashing light on the fins, the team controlled the robot's direction and speed in a watery maze. The research demonstrated that this thin, two-dimensional design is a foundation for more efficient biohybrid robots. The study explored optimizing the gel's properties and groove shapes to maximize muscle force production.
items.audio_script: From MIT News - Robotics, "Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze". This report details the development of a soft, muscle-powered swimming robot utilizing a thin film of gel and genetically engineered muscle cells to propel itself through water. The research involved engineering muscle cells to respond to light stimuli, causing the robot's fins to flap and generate propulsion. Flashing light directed at the fins allowed the team to control the robot's movement and speed within a watery maze. The study further explored optimizing the gel's properties and groove shapes to maximize muscle force generation, establishing a foundation for more efficient biohybrid robots. This work suggests a pathway toward developing highly efficient, biologically inspired robotic systems.

items.title: Delta Intelligence Targets Energy and Infrastructure Beyond Its Household Robot Demo
items.summary: Delta Intelligence's initial demonstration focused on household tasks, but founder Xiaojian Ma prioritizes energy and infrastructure as near-term deployment targets. The company is developing a head-and-backpack system to integrate models onto various humanoid platforms. Whole-body data collection was planned from the start, emphasizing the need to capture coordination beyond just the hands. Future plans involve scaling pretraining data, improving reinforcement learning, and conducting outdoor testing in harsh environments. The ultimate goal is to prove the demonstrated coordination can translate into reliable work in energy and infrastructure settings.
